Conduct a low‑cost purchase‑intent test to validate demand before full rollout. Target customer: Homeowners with small gardens who need a single, easy‑to‑use machine for lawn care.. Value proposition: A differentiated lawn tractor that combines Deere's tractor engineering with a consumer‑friendly design, offering convenience, durability, and a premium price point through the existing dealer network.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed purchase‑intent test (500 respondents, 6 weeks, €15,000) to measure homeowner vs small‑farm purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium.. Uncertainty: The size of the homeowner market in 1962 is unknown; competitive lawn tractors may have already captured demand; small‑farm owner demand is uncertain.. Would change if: If the test shows small‑farm owners showing higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium than homeowners, we would reconsider targeting small‑farm owners instead.; If no test is run, we would remain uncertain about whether a differentiated proposition would generate measurable demand.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Hellberg Safety investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current hearing-protection offering.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate demand, willingness to pay, or a clear path to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must be based on observable data, not assumptions.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, construction, or home improvement) with a new product or marketing approach.; 2) Expand the existing hearing-protection line into adjacent consumer segments (e.g., fashion, lifestyle, or health) without a differentiated proposition.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing on the current hearing and face protection portfolio and existing B2B/industrial customers.; 4) Change the route to market or customer group (e.g., selling directly to consumers online, partnering with retailers, or targeting a new demographic) without altering the product.; 5) No expansion: maintain the current product mix and market focus, and not pursue new consumer propositions..

T1: Consumers treat hearing protection as a medical necessity and will purchase it for workplace compliance and health protection, so a manufacturer can capture value by offering EN 352 certified products at premium prices. Who benefits: Individual consumers need compliance for workplaces and health protection, and manufacturers benefit from higher margins.. Why behaviour changes: Regulatory requirements (e.g., EN 352) and awareness of hearing damage change consumer perception from optional to necessary.. How value is captured: Premium pricing for certified products and brand trust in safety compliance.. Assumptions: Regulatory requirements will remain unchanged or increase in target markets.; Consumers are aware of and willing to pay for hearing protection standards.; Hellberg can produce and market certified products efficiently.. Predictions: Willingness to pay for EN 352 certification will be higher than for non-certified products.; Sales of certified hearing protection will grow in regions with strong workplace and health regulations.; Competitors without certification will see reduced market share..

T2: Consumers treat hearing protection as a fashion accessory and will purchase multiple styles for personal expression, so a manufacturer can capture value by offering a diverse, design-led consumer line. Who benefits: Individual consumers seeking personal style and multiple uses, and manufacturers benefit from higher-margin lifestyle products.. Why behaviour changes: Social media influence and lifestyle branding shift consumer perception from functional to expressive, leading to multiple purchases.. How value is captured: Premium pricing for design-led products and brand extension across multiple use cases.. Assumptions: Fashion and lifestyle trends will continue to drive consumer purchases of safety gear.; Consumers are willing to pay for unique, design-focused hearing protection.; Hellberg can adapt its manufacturing and marketing to a lifestyle brand.. Predictions: Sales of design-led hearing protection will increase in regions with strong fashion and lifestyle culture.; Consumers will purchase multiple styles rather than a single product.; Brand awareness will rise among younger, fashion-conscious demographics..

Test "Consumer Proposition Test: Workplace vs Fashion Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated product offers and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 from industrial/construction workplaces (targeting T1) and 250 from fashion/lifestyle consumers (targeting T2). Recruit via panels to match demographics.. Measure: Average WTP in euros for a hypothetical EN 352-certified hearing protection product, and binary choice: would purchase for workplace vs fashion use.. Predictions: T1: Workplace group will show higher average WTP and higher purchase intent than fashion group.; T2: Fashion group will show higher average WTP and higher purchase intent than workplace group.. Decision rule: If workplace group average WTP exceeds fashion group by at least €10, proceed with workplace-focused differentiated proposition. If fashion group average WTP exceeds workplace by at least €10, proceed with fashion-focused proposition. If the difference is below €10, no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition yet. Public evidence shows EN 352 certification exists and is used in some regions, but it does not demonstrate consumer willingness to pay for it or the size of the market. A low-cost test (e.g., willingness-to-pay survey) is needed before committing resources. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated result SYN-C concerns wear frequency based on appearance and does not address consumer willingness to pay for EN 352 certification or market size. Therefore it does not affect T1. New claim: Consumers treat hearing protection as a medical necessity and will purchase it for workplace compliance and health protection, so a manufacturer can capture value by offering EN 352 certified products at premium prices.. Evidence: SYN-C.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition yet. Public evidence shows EN 352 certification exists and is used in some regions, but it does not demonstrate consumer willingness to pay for it or the size of the market. A low-cost test (e.g., willingness-to-pay survey) is needed before committing resources. Target customer: Industrial/construction workers and their employers in regions with strong workplace and health regulations.. Value proposition: EN 352-certified hearing protection that meets regulatory requirements and provides peace of mind for workplaces and health protection.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Proposition Test: Workplace vs Fashion Messaging to measure willingness to pay for workplace-focused versus fashion-focused differentiated proposition.. Uncertainty: Consumer willingness to pay for EN 352 certification and the size of the market are uncertain. Evidence does not show demand or price sensitivity.. Would change if: If the test shows the fashion group achieving at least €10 higher average willingness to pay than the workplace group, we would shift focus to a fashion-led differentiated proposition.; If the test shows no significant difference or the fashion group winning, we would recommend no expansion and maintain the current portfolio.. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive hearing protection as a lifestyle or fashion accessory, because they are willing to pay a premium for style and comfort. Who benefits: Consumers seeking comfortable, stylish earplugs for recreational activities and fashion-conscious individuals.. Why behaviour changes: When hearing protection is framed as a fashion item, consumers shift from utilitarian use to multiple purchases for different settings, increasing repeat purchases.. How value is captured: Hellberg can capture value through premium pricing, design-led product lines, and direct-to-consumer or retail partnerships that emphasize aesthetics.. Assumptions: Consumers currently view hearing protection as purely functional.; Fashion and lifestyle influence purchase decisions for earplugs.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for stylish, comfortable earplugs.. Predictions: In a test offering a stylish, comfortable earplug at a premium price, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard industrial earplug.; Consumers will report higher willingness to purchase multiple pairs for different activities.; Sales will be driven by fashion and lifestyle messaging rather than purely functional positioning..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive hearing protection as a health necessity, because they are willing to pay for proven protection against noise-induced hearing loss. Who benefits: Health-conscious consumers, parents of children, and individuals at high risk of hearing damage.. Why behaviour changes: When hearing protection is framed as a medical necessity, consumers shift from utilitarian use to consistent use across activities, reducing the need for multiple products.. How value is captured: Hellberg can capture value through premium positioning, health messaging, and partnerships with healthcare providers or insurance companies that emphasize protection.. Assumptions: Consumers currently view hearing protection as optional.; Health concerns drive purchase decisions for earplugs.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for products marketed as medical necessity.. Predictions: In a test offering a health-focused earplug at a premium price, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard industrial earplug.; Consumers will report higher intent to use the product consistently across activities.; Sales will be driven by health messaging rather than fashion or lifestyle positioning..

Test "Consumer Proposition Test: Health vs. Fashion Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging and choice-based conjoint. Participants are recruited from two segments: (1) health-conscious adults (n=300) who currently purchase hearing protection for work/industrial use; (2) fashion-conscious adults (n=300) who view safety gear as an accessory. Each segment sees one product description: health-focused (EN 352 certification, hearing health benefits) vs. fashion-focused (stylish design, comfort, lifestyle integration). Participants then choose which product they would purchase and indicate maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 300 health-conscious adults and 300 fashion-conscious adults, recruited via an online panel to ensure demographic representation.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and maximum price willingness to pay (continuous). Secondary measure: primary purchase reason (open-ended).. Predictions: T1: Health-focused segment will show purchase intent at least 15% higher than fashion-focused segment, and willingness to pay will be at least 10% higher for the health product.; T2: Fashion-focused segment will show purchase intent at least 15% higher than health-focused segment, and willingness to pay will be at least 10% higher for the fashion product.. Decision rule: If the health-focused segment's purchase intent exceeds the fashion-focused segment's by at least 15 percentage points AND the maximum price willingness to pay for the health product is at least 10% higher than for the fashion product, proceed with a differentiated health proposition. If the fashion-focused segment's purchase intent exceeds the health-focused segment by at least 15 percentage points AND the maximum price willingness to pay for the fashion product is at least 10% higher, proceed with a differentiated fashion proposition. If neither condition is met, do not expand.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Public evidence shows EN 352 certification exists and is used in some consumer products, but it does not demonstrate consumer willingness to pay a premium or that they purchase for non-work use. A low-cost test (e.g., a choice-based conjoint) is needed to measure demand before committing resources. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

Target customer: Health-conscious adults who currently purchase hearing protection for work/industrial use, as they are already familiar with certification and regulatory requirements..
